name: Second Entry (H2/L2) pull-back
description: Two-legged pull-back continuation strategy: EMA(20) trend, a failed first break (H1/L1), a deeper pull-back, then the second break as entry, gated by a Fair Value Gap and a trend/ADX filter, with a fixed 2R target.

rules.trend: close > EMA(20) = bull regime, close < EMA(20) = bear regime
rules.leg1_H1: first break of prior bar's high during a pull-back (recorded, not traded)
rules.leg2_H2: after a deeper pull-back extreme than the pre-H1 extreme, the next break is the signal
gates: bar quality: signal bar closes with the break, in the upper/lower half of its range (>= close_pos_ratio)
EMA touch: pull-back came within ema_touch_points of the EMA
trend filter: EMA slope over trend_lookback_bars in trade direction AND ADX >= adx_min_level
FVG: signal candle or the candle right after it is the impulse (middle) bar of a 3-candle Fair Value Gap
rules.entry: buy-stop at H2 high + buffer / sell-stop at L2 low - buffer

methodology: forward-replay vs real bar highs/lows; SL-first on ties; pending order expires if unfilled in 12 bars, then held to real SL/TP (no time stop); NO look-ahead — FVG is a fixed 3-candle pattern (no repaint) and fills start two bars after the signal (after the gap-confirming bar closes); NO spread/slippage/commission modelled

intraday_timeframe_study_2015_2025.note: M3 leads on raw edge (both total R and expectancy) but has the tightest stops (~11 pips) so is the most cost-sensitive; M15 is the most robust to spread. Choose per your broker's real intraday costs.

status: PROVISIONAL — positive expectancy on historical mid-price data across all pairs and timeframes, now measured with trades held to real SL/TP (no artificial time-out). Still NOT validated with transaction costs or out-of-sample. Not confirmed as a tradeable edge.

execution.note: M3 is the default because it led on both total R and expectancy in the corrected study; it also has the tightest stops so is the most cost-sensitive. Switch the bot's EXEC_TF to M5/M15 for a more spread-robust run.
